claim: Deolalikar's finite-model-theory reduction is justified in restricting general polynomial-time FO(LFP) computations to monadic fixed points over a successor structure.

evidence.locator: Deolalikar 2010 p.67 as quoted in Neil Immerman's letter, Lipton blog 2010-08-12
evidence.text: The claimed reduction relies on FO(LFP) capturing polynomial-time queries over a successor relation, while the paper then restricts the fixed point to monadic relations.

evidence.locator: Neil Immerman, reproduced by Richard Lipton, 2010-08-12 paragraphs 'other problem'
evidence.text: The product-space monadic encoding requires higher-arity incidence relations to access tuple coordinates; these change the locality properties. With only monadic fixed points and successor, the restricted logic does not express all of P.

evidence.locator: Immerman, same letter, paragraphs on ordering
evidence.text: Transitive closure of successor can build a linear order by LFP, carrying order-dependent intermediate information. An order-invariant final property does not force all stages to be order invariant.

claim: If a least-fixed-point computation produces an order-invariant final query, every intermediate fixed-point stage must be order invariant.

evidence.locator: Neil Immerman in Lipton, 2010-08-12, successor example
evidence.text: The transitive closure of a successor relation can be built using least fixed points. Intermediate stages depend on that supplied successor order even when the final queried property is order invariant.

evidence.locator: Deolalikar step as described by Immerman, 2010-08-12
evidence.text: The disputed argument inferred invariance of each LFP stage from the final SAT query's order invariance, then invoked Gaifman locality.

claim: Kempe's 1879 degree-five recolouring step proves that a central pentagonal region can always be freed by treating the necessary Kempe-chain switches as independent.

evidence.locator: Georges Gonthier, A computer-checked proof of the Four Colour Theorem, printed p.7
evidence.text: The degree-five step uses local interchanges in two-colour chains around a central pentagon; it assumes enumerated chain patterns exhaust the possibilities.

evidence.locator: Gonthier, printed p.7, paragraph following step (f)
evidence.text: Cases were missing from the enumeration. Swapping colours in one chain can disrupt other chains; the claimed extension to the pentagon therefore fails.

evidence.locator: Heawood 1890 counterexample, MathWorld Heawood Four-Color Map
evidence.text: Heawood's map is a counterexample to Kempe's particular proof procedure, not to the four-colour theorem itself.

claim: The historical failure of Kempe's pentagon step leaves the earlier recolouring arguments for faces with at most four sides intact.

evidence.locator: Gonthier, A computer-checked proof, printed p.7, step (e)
evidence.text: For a minimal hypothetical counterexample, a central face other than a pentagon can be recoloured immediately (with two opposite sides erased in the square case).

evidence.locator: St Andrews MacTutor, Alfred Kempe biography, section on four colours
evidence.text: Kempe's reducibility criterion for configurations with at most four neighbours was valid; the error concerned extension to five-neighbour configurations.

claim: Lamé's 1847 factorization of x^p+y^p in cyclotomic integers establishes Fermat's Last Theorem for all odd prime exponents because those integers always have unique prime factorization.

evidence.locator: MacTutor, Fermat's last theorem history, 1847 section
evidence.text: Lamé announced a general proof using linear factorization over cyclotomic integers. Liouville immediately identified the assumed uniqueness of prime factorization.

evidence.locator: Mathematical Association of America, Algebraic Number Theory and Fermat's Last Theorem, Lamé discussion
evidence.text: The inference that each relatively prime factor of a prime power is itself an appropriate power requires unique factorization. General cyclotomic integer rings do not always have it.

evidence.locator: MacTutor, 1847 section, Kummer letter
evidence.text: Kummer's earlier work demonstrated failure of unique factorization for some cyclotomic integers, and ideal numbers supplied an alternative algebraic framework.

claim: For odd prime p and a primitive pth root of unity ζ, the polynomial identity x^p+y^p = ∏_(i=0)^(p−1) (x+ζ^i y) is valid in the cyclotomic ring.

evidence.locator: MAA, Algebraic Number Theory and Fermat's Last Theorem, Lamé factorization
evidence.text: Lamé correctly used the splitting of x^p+y^p into p linear terms over Z[ζ].

evidence.locator: Elementary factorization check
evidence.text: The p roots of X^p+ y^p for odd p are −ζ^i y. Both sides are monic degree-p polynomials with those roots, so their equality is a valid identity independent of unique factorization into primes.

claim: The Euler-system extension used in Wiles's June 1993 Fermat announcement was already complete as presented, without a gap.

evidence.locator: Andrew Wiles, Annals of Mathematics 141 (1995), printed p.453, autobiographical account
evidence.text: Wiles says the Euler-system construction extending Flach's method became clearly incomplete and possibly flawed in autumn 1993.

evidence.locator: Wiles, same printed p.453, January–September 1994 account
evidence.text: Wiles and Richard Taylor attempted repairs, then pivoted to the earlier deformation-ring approach and auxiliary-prime patching after the September 19, 1994 insight.

claim: The published 1995 Wiles proof uses a different, repaired complete-intersection argument involving auxiliary primes and Taylor–Wiles patching.

evidence.locator: Andrew Wiles, Annals of Mathematics 141 (1995), printed p.453
evidence.text: Wiles reports replacing the attempted Euler-system extension with a gluing argument for Hecke rings using auxiliary primes; he refers the full construction and complete-intersection deduction to the Taylor–Wiles companion paper.

evidence.locator: Wiles, Annals of Mathematics 141 (1995), printed p.443 abstract and pp.443–444 introduction
evidence.text: The published paper states that semistable elliptic curves over Q are modular and that Fermat's Last Theorem follows by Frey–Serre–Ribet.

evidence.locator: Publication status, Annals of Mathematics 141 (1995), pp.443–551
evidence.text: This claim concerns the corrected published 1995 argument, not a retroactive validation of the June 1993 gap.

claim: The identity F_(n+1) = F'_n \ A' used in Ansari's Lemma 3.1 holds at the induction stage n=1.

evidence.locator: Mohammad Ansari, NNTDM 31(3) (2025), printed p.477, formula (1)
evidence.text: F2 has two ternary digits a0,a1 both in {0,1} and elements m=4k+3. For 0≤k<9 this gives m in {3,7,15,19}.

evidence.locator: Ansari, printed p.478, definitions of F'_n and A' in Lemma 3.1
evidence.text: F'_1 permits two ternary digits a0,a1 in {0,1,2}; the removed subset A' uses both high digits equal to 2. In the first block this leaves {3,7,11,15,19,23,27,31}.

evidence.locator: Finite witness from the printed definitions
evidence.text: m=11 corresponds to k=2, ternary digits (a1,a0)=(0,2); it belongs to F'_1 \ A' but not F2. Thus the displayed equality used by the induction is false. This refutes that particular sieve argument, not Collatz convergence.

claim: For a recursively sufficient set F, if every element of F up to N reaches 1, strong induction establishes that every positive integer up to N reaches 1.

evidence.locator: Ansari, NNTDM 31(3) (2025), printed p.473, Definition 1.3
evidence.text: Recursive sufficiency requires that each n>1 outside F merge under Collatz iteration with some positive m<n.

evidence.locator: Ansari, printed pp.474–475, Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 2.1
evidence.text: An induction on n invokes the smaller merged integer when n is outside F. Members of F are covered by the hypothesis, so the finite verification transfer follows from the definition.

evidence.locator: Scope control
evidence.text: The result is conditional on the recursive-sufficiency property of F. It does not establish convergence for all integers without verifying the condition or supplying the required set.
